# Kay

> Kay is a Bun web framework. A `.kay` file is one component: TypeScript fences, then a pug-like indented template. It compiles to TSX, runs on Solid 2, and is served by an Elysia plugin with server rendering and automatic islands. Everything is typed, templates included, and `kay check` reports errors at the `.kay` line and column.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- Every dynamic value sits in `{}`: `a(href={url})`, `p Hello {name}`. A static attribute value is a quoted string: `a(href="/about")`.
- Signals are explicit. Read `count()`, write `count.set(1)` or `count.set(c => c + 1)`. Props and server data are plain names, never called: `{title}`, not `{title()}`.
- Every `for` has a `key={...}`.
- The component script exports types only. Shared values live in `.ts` modules.
- A page has no props: its data comes from its `--- server` fence.
- Indentation is spaces only, consistent within a block. Text after a tag needs one space: `p Hello`, never `p:Hello`.
- Pug features that do not exist: `- code` lines, `#{}` and `!{}` interpolation, `+mixins`, `include`, `extends`, `block`, filters, `&attributes`, `case`, `each`, `while`.

## File layout

Up to two fences come first, in either order, then the template. Both are optional.

```kay
--- server
const greeting = 'Hello'
---
---
import { signal } from 'kay'

const count = signal(0)
---
p {greeting}
button(onClick={() => count.set(c => c + 1)}) Clicked {count()} times
```

- `---` holds the component script: imports, props, signals, functions. It runs wherever the component renders.
- `--- server` exists on pages and layouts only. It runs on the server for each request and never reaches the browser.

## Component script

Props are declared once, at the top level, with the `props<T>()` macro. It needs no import.

```kay
---
import type { Todo } from './todo'

const { todo, size = 'md', onToggle } = props<{ todo: Todo, size?: 'sm' | 'md', onToggle?: (id: number) => void }>()
---
li(class={size})
  input(type="checkbox" checked={todo.done} onChange={() => onToggle?.(todo.id)})
  span {todo.title}
```

- Destructure one level deep and read nested fields as `todo.title`; give defaults in the destructuring. `const all = props<T>()` also works and reads as `all.todo`.
- Props stay reactive: the compiler turns each destructured name into a live read. They are read-only.
- `signal(value)` from `kay` makes state; `signal<T>()` starts as `undefined`. Derived values are plain functions: `const shown = () => todos.filter(t => !t.done)`.
- Other Solid primitives come from `solid-js`.

## Template lines

Each line is one of the following; deeper indentation nests children under the line above.

| Line | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `tag.class#id(attributes) text` | An element. Each part is optional, but the line starts with a tag, `.` or `#`. |
| `.card` | A `div`: a line starting with `.` or `#` has an implied `div`. |
| `Card(title="x")` | A component: a capitalised tag, imported in the script. |
| `\| text {expr}` | A text line, also the way to put a lone `{expr}` on its own line. |
| `// note` | A comment. Lines indented under it are commented out too. |
| `if cond` / `else if cond` / `else` | Conditional rendering. |
| `if user() as u` | Binds the truthy value to `u` for the children. |
| `for item of list key={item.id}` | A keyed list. `else` right after it renders when the list is empty. |
| `for item, i of list key={i}` | Rows matched by position. |
| `slot` | Where a layout or wrapper renders its children. |
| `@name` | Directly under a component: passes the indented block as its `name` prop. |
| `head` | At the top level: its `title`, `meta`, `link`, `style`, `script` and `base` children go in the document head. |

```kay
---
import type { Todo } from './todo'
import { signal } from 'kay'
import TodoItem from './todo-item.kay'

const { todos } = props<{ todos: Todo[] }>()
const filter = signal('')
const selected = signal<Todo>()
const shown = () => todos.filter(todo => todo.title.includes(filter()))
---
section.todo-list
  input(type="search" bind:value={filter} placeholder="Filter")
  ul
    for todo, i of shown() key={todo.id}
      TodoItem(todo={todo} index={i} onToggle={id => selected.set(todos.find(t => t.id === id))})
    else
      li.empty Nothing matches
  if selected() as todo
    p Selected #[strong {todo.title}]
```

### Elements

- Classes: `.class` takes Tailwind names, `:`, `/`, `@` and `!` included: `div.md:flex.w-1/2.hover:underline`. A class holding `.` or `[` goes in `class="..."`.
- `class={...}` takes a string, an array or a `{ name: boolean }` object, and merges with the `.class` shorthand. An element has one `class` attribute and one id.
- Attributes are separated by spaces, inside one pair of parentheses that may span lines: `a(href="/x" target="_blank")`. A value is a quoted string or `{expression}`. A name alone is a boolean attribute. `{...obj}` spreads.
- Events are camelCase handlers: `onClick={save}`, `onInput={e => name.set(e.currentTarget.value)}`.
- `bind:value={signal}` on `input`, `textarea` and `select`, and `bind:checked={signal}` on a checkbox, read and write a signal both ways.
- `ref={el => ...}` receives the DOM element.
- Inline text follows the tag after one space. `\{` and `\#` are a literal brace and hash.
- `#[tag inline]` puts an element inside text: `p Read #[a(href="/docs") the docs] first`.
- `tag: child` nests one element on the same line: `li: a(href="/") Home`.

### Slots

```kay
---
import type { JSX } from '@solidjs/web'

const { title, actions } = props<{ title: string, actions?: JSX.Element }>()
---
article.card
  header
    h2 {title}
    | {actions}
  slot
```

A parent fills it like this: the `@actions` block becomes the `actions` prop and the other children go to `slot`.

```kay
---
import Card from './card.kay'
---
Card(title="Todos")
  @actions
    a(href="/new") New
  p Body text
```

### Head

```kay
--- server
import { findTodo } from '../../data'

const todo = await findTodo(Number(ctx.params.id)) ?? ctx.notFound()
---
head
  title {todo.title} | Todos
  meta(name="description" content={`Todo #${todo.id}`})
h1 {todo.title}
```

- One `head` block per template, at its top level, in a page, a layout or a static component; an island has none.
- The page wins over its layouts: one `title`, and one `meta` per `name`, `property` or `http-equiv`. A `link` is one per `rel` and `href`.
- Head elements hold text only. The default charset and viewport tags can be replaced the same way.

## Styles

A component script or any `.ts` module imports its stylesheet: `import './card.css'`. Each page links one stylesheet per layout, outermost first, then its own, holding the CSS of every component it renders, islands included. Bun bundles them: `@import`, nesting and relative `url()` assets work, and `url(/logo.png)` is left for a public file.

Tailwind runs as a build plugin. `bun add -d tailwindcss bun-plugin-tailwind`, then:

```ts
import tailwind from 'bun-plugin-tailwind'
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [tailwind] })
```

`src/app.css`, imported by the root `_layout.kay`, points Tailwind at the classes kay collects from the `.class` shorthand, which it cannot read off `div.md:flex.w-1/2` itself:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@source '../.kay/classes.txt';
```

## Public files

Files in `public/` (the `publicDir` option) are served at their path as they are: `public/robots.txt` at `/robots.txt`. A file sharing its path with a page stops the server at boot.

## Islands

A component is interactive when any element in it has an `on*` handler, a `bind:` or a `ref`, or when its script imports a value from `kay` or `solid-js`, such as `signal`. An interactive component renders on the server and hydrates in the browser as an island; everything else ships no JavaScript. Interactive components rendered inside an island are part of it.

Props a static component passes to an island travel as JSON, so `kay check` rejects functions, Dates, Maps, Sets and class instances there. Children cannot cross either: rendering an island with children from a static parent throws.

An island hydrates as soon as the page loads, its chunks preloaded. `hydrate="idle"` waits until the browser is idle and `hydrate="visible"` until it scrolls near the viewport, neither preloaded: `Comments(postId={post.id} hydrate="visible")`. Only an island takes `hydrate`, and only from a static parent.

## Pages and routing

Pages live in `src/routes/`:

| File | URL |
| --- | --- |
| `index.kay` | `/` |
| `about.kay` | `/about` |
| `todos/[id].kay` | `/todos/:id`, read as `ctx.params.id` |
| `docs/[...path].kay` | `/docs/*`, read as `ctx.params.path` |
| `_layout.kay` | Wraps every page in its directory and below, outermost first, rendering the page at its `slot`. |
| `_404.kay` | Rendered with status 404 for `ctx.notFound()` in its directory and below; the root one also answers URLs no page serves. |
| `_error.kay` | Rendered with status 500 when a load or render throws, and for 404s with no `_404.kay`. |

Other files starting with `_` are not routes. Every top-level name the server fence declares reaches the template, typed. The fence may use top-level `await` and the `ctx` object:

- `ctx.params`, typed from the file name, `ctx.url`, `ctx.request`
- `ctx.cookies`, a `Bun.CookieMap`: `ctx.cookies.get('theme')`; what `set` and `delete` change is sent back, redirects included
- `ctx.locals`, what the app's Elysia `derive`, `resolve` and `decorate` add, such as the signed-in user
- `ctx.status(404)` and `ctx.headers` set the response
- `ctx.redirect('/login')` and `ctx.notFound()` stop rendering

Layout and page loads run in parallel; when several fail, the outermost one decides the response.

The nearest special page wins, wrapped by the layouts of its own directory. `_error.kay` reads `ctx.error`: `status`, `message` and, in development only, `stack`. Logged and displayed stacks point at `.kay` lines. In production the message is generic and the real error goes to `console.error`; without an `_error.kay` the response is plain text, and development shows the stack instead.

```kay
--- server
const { status, message } = ctx.error
---
h1 Error {status}
p {message}
```

```kay
--- server
import { findTodo } from '../../data'

const id = Number(ctx.params.id)
const todo = await findTodo(id) ?? ctx.notFound()
---
h1 {todo.title}
p.status {todo.done ? 'Done' : 'Open'}
```

## Actions

A page's server fence exports actions: an Elysia schema and a handler. Each one becomes `POST /_kay/action/<file>/<name>`, with its input validated.

```kay
--- server
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { action } from 'kay'
import { addTodo, listTodos } from '../data'

export const add = action(t.Object({ title: t.String({ minLength: 1, error: 'Write a title' }) }), async ({ title }, ctx) => {
  if ((await listTodos()).some(todo => todo.title === title))
    return ctx.fail(409, { message: 'Already on the list' })

  return (await addTodo(title)).id
})

const todos = await listTodos()
const failure = ctx.failed(add)
---
ul
  for todo of todos key={todo.id}
    li: a(href={`/todos/${todo.id}`}) {todo.title}
form(action={add})
  input(name="title" placeholder="New todo" value={failure?.values.title})
  if failure?.errors.title as message
    p.error {message}
  if failure?.data as data
    p.error {data.message}
  button Add
```

- `form(action={add})` posts without JavaScript; `kay check` verifies every field `name` against the schema. After the post the browser goes back to the page, or wherever the handler's `ctx.redirect` points.
- A post the schema refuses, or whose handler returns `ctx.fail(status, data)`, goes back to the page too. There `ctx.failed(add)` returns `{ status, values, errors, data }`, typed from the action, or `undefined`: `values` is what the form posted (fields named like a password left out), `errors` a message per refused field, the schema's `error` option when set, and `data` what `ctx.fail` received. It is read on that one render only.
- An island imports the action from the page and calls it: `import { add } from '../routes/index.kay'`, then `const id = await add({ title })`. The call is typed, `ctx.fail` results excluded, and throws `ActionError` with `status`, `errors` and `data` when it fails.
- A handler that throws answers 500 with a generic message and logs the error.
- The handler's second argument has `request`, `cookies`, `locals`, `status(code)`, `headers`, `redirect(location)` and `fail(status, data)`.

## Locals and guards

`ctx.locals` is the Elysia context of the request. Declare what the app adds once, in a `.ts` module, and register its type:

```ts
import type { LocalsOf } from 'kay'
import { Elysia } from 'elysia'

export const auth = new Elysia({ name: 'auth' }).derive({ as: 'scoped' }, async ({ cookie }) => ({ user: await findSession(cookie.session?.value) }))

declare module 'kay' {
  interface Register {
    locals: LocalsOf<typeof auth>
  }
}
```

A guard is an Elysia `onBeforeHandle` registered before `.use(await pages())`: it covers pages and actions alike. A layout's `ctx.redirect` is no guard, since actions never run layout loads.

```ts
new Elysia()
  .use(auth)
  .onBeforeHandle(({ user, path, redirect }) => user === undefined && path.startsWith('/account') ? redirect('/login') : undefined)
  .use(await pages())
  .listen(3000)
```

## What `kay check` verifies

- Every expression, prop and server name, as TypeScript does.
- `a(href="/todos/1")` and template literals such as `` `/todos/${id}` `` against the routes; a plain `string`, relative paths, `//host` and other schemes are not checked.
- Form field names against the action schema.
- Island props passed from static components are JSON-serializable.

## Project setup

`kay new my-app` writes a project that already checks, builds and runs: this setup, a layout, a page, a `_404.kay` and an island. By hand, the server entry is:

```ts
import { Elysia } from 'elysia'
import { pages } from 'kay/server'

new Elysia().use(await pages()).listen(3000)
```

Project settings live in an optional `kay.config.ts` at the root, read by `pages()` and every command; options passed to `pages()` win over it.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'kay/server'

export default defineConfig({ routes: 'src/routes', lang: 'en', minify: true, plugins: [] })
```

`pages()` also takes `root`, `dev` (default: `NODE_ENV` is `development`) and `prebuilt` (default: `NODE_ENV` is `production`), which serves what `kay build` wrote instead of bundling at boot. A `.ts` file imports a component as `import Card from './card.kay'`, typed through the generated `.kay/types` tree. List `.kay/` in `.gitignore` and merge the tree in `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "@solidjs/web",
    "module": "Preserve",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "rootDirs": [".", ".kay/types"],
    "strict": true
  },
  "include": ["src", ".kay/types"]
}
```

## Commands

- `kay new <dir> [--kay <dependency>]`: scaffold a project in an empty directory; `--kay` sets the `kay` dependency, a packed copy of this checkout by default.
- `kay dev [entry]`: run the server entry (default `src/server.ts`) with `NODE_ENV=development`, restarting it on every change; open pages reload by themselves, and a project that fails to compile shows its errors in the browser.
- `kay build [dir]`: bundle the islands for production, minified, into `.kay/client`; then start the server with `NODE_ENV=production`. Each page preloads the chunks of the islands it renders.
- `kay check [dir] [-p tsconfig.json]`: type-check the project, `.kay` files included.
- `kay fmt [paths...] [--check]`: format `.kay` files; `--check` lists unformatted files and fails.
- `kay lsp --stdio`: the language server behind the editor extension in `editors/vscode`.
